title: Token Governance: structured rotation & per-scope API key model
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a first-class API token governance system as part of the Admin Controls initiative. Scope covers token naming conventions, per-scope (least-privilege) keys, rotation workflows (manual + automated), expiry TTLs, audit logging for all lifecycle events, and admin UI/CLI support. This work ties into RBAC v2 (scopes map to role capabilities) and must interoperate with SSO/SAML constraints for admin-level operations.

Main objectives:
- Enforce and onboard a per-scope API key model to reduce blast radius.
- Provide standard rotation endpoints and optional automated rotation for service keys.
- Default expiry policy, with exceptions for long-lived machine-to-machine tokens after approval.
- Strong audit logging for create/rotate/revoke/expiry with immutable event stream.
- Admin UI & Console actions controlled via SSO (SAML) and require MFA for privileged operations.

Design constraints & non-goals:
- Not addressing user session tokens or OAuth flows in this ticket (separate workstream).
- Backwards-compatible enforcement strategy: gradually enable hard expiry via feature flag.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
1) New token model persists: name, scope(s) (comma-separated), created_by, created_at, expires_at, rotated_from_id, status, rotation_count, last_used_at.
2) API accepts per-scope keys and rejects actions outside declared scopes with 403 and a structured error.
3) Default expiry applied on creation (90 days) unless request includes approved exception tag.
4) Rotation endpoint (/admin/tokens/:id/rotate) issues new key, marks old key rotated, and emits detailed audit event.
5) All token lifecycle events are written into the audit stream (Kafka topic security.audits) and are visible in the Console audit viewer within 5 minutes.
6) Admin Console shows key metadata, masked secret, last used, and a rotate/revoke workflow gated by SSO session + MFA.
7) Migration plan documented and tested in staging; existing keys are marked with 'legacy:true' and given soft expiry warnings for 30 days.

Implementation notes:
- DB: add columns to tokens table: name (string), scopes (string), expires_at (timestamp), rotated_from_id (uuid), rotation_count (int), status (enum), last_used_at (timestamp), legacy (bool). Add index on hashed_secret and last_used_at.
- Secrets: never store raw token; store HMAC of token for lookup, KDF for long-term hashes. Use KMS for key encryption at rest.
- API layer: middleware to check expiry and scope membership. Return structured error codes for audit ingestion.
- Background jobs: daily job to emit expiry-notifications, prune expired tokens and increment rotation_count metrics.
- Audit: events must include actor_id, actor_auth_method (SSO/API), action (create/rotate/revoke/expire/use), token_id (opaque), correlation_id, client_ip, user_agent. Events pushed to Kafka and archived to S3 for compliance retention.
- Console: admin-only flows require SSO session; add UX for token naming with suggested pattern: team:purpose:env:YYYYMMDD. Provide 'create token' wizard with scope picker and TTL dropdown.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged backend + Console in staging.
2) Generate migration tool to tag existing tokens as legacy and set soft expiry warnings (2 weeks).
3) Open beta with selected internal teams; monitor token usage and error rates.
4) Enforce hard expiry after 30 days by toggling feature flag and sending customer notifications.

Migration & customer communication:
- Bulk tool to mint per-scope tokens on behalf of customers (admin-consent required).
- Automated emails and usage dashboards for tokens nearing soft expiry.
- Support playbook for enterprise customers requiring exceptions (support ticket + audit log).

Trade-offs considered:
- Shorter TTL (e.g., 30d) improves security but increases developer friction; chose 90d default to balance.
- Per-scope keys reduce blast radius at cost of increased token count; provide tooling to bulk-generate scopes.
- Immediate rotation on compromise vs. gradual revocation: rotation API supports atomic swap for services, and revoke endpoint supports immediate cut-off for user keys.
